        14                  THE SECRETARY:    By Senator Dilan,

        15       Legislative Resolution Number 207, mourning

        16       the death of Boxing Hall of Famer and

        17       Ambassador Jose Torres, distinguished citizen

        18       and devoted member of his community.

        19                  "WHEREAS, It is the custom of this

        20       Legislative Body to pay tribute to citizens of

        21       the State of New York whose lifework and civic

        22       endeavor serve to enhance the quality of life

        23       in their communities and the great state of

        24       New York; and



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         241



         1                  "WHEREAS, Jose 'Chegui' Torres, a

         2       former light-heavyweight champion who became a

         3       boxing official and a literary presence in the

         4       sport as a biographer of Muhammad Ali and Mike

         5       Tyson, died on Monday, January 19, 2009, in

         6       Ponce, Puerto Rico, at age 72; and

         7                  "WHEREAS, Revered both in Spanish

         8       Harlem and in Puerto Rico, Jose Torres was one

         9       of New York's renaissance men:  world champion

        10       athlete, trendsetter, journalist and author;

        11       and

        12                  "WHEREAS, Fighting professionally

        13       from 1958 to 1969, Jose Torres had a record of

        14       41-3-1.  He captured the light-heavyweight

        15       crown in March of 1965 when the referee

        16       stopped his fight with Willie Pastrano after

        17       the ninth round.  After three title defenses,

        18       he lost the championship to Dick Tiger of

        19       Nigeria on a decision in December of 1966; and

        20                  "WHEREAS, Jose Torres was inducted

        21       into the International Boxing Hall of Fame in

        22       1997.  He was the chairman of the New York

        23       State Athletic Commission from 1984 to 1988,

        24       becoming the first former professional boxer



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         242



         1       and the first Latino to head the agency, which

         2       oversees boxing in the state; and

         3                  "WHEREAS, Jose Torres was the

         4       author of Sting Like a Bee:  The Muhammad Ali 

         5       Story (1971) and Fire and Fear:  The Inside 

         6       Story of Mike Tyson (1989), and he wrote for

         7       the New York Post and the New York newspaper

         8       El Diario La Prensa.  Jose Torres, a native of

         9       the Ponce, Puerto Rico area and the son of a

        10       businessman, learned to box in the Army and

        11       captured the light-middleweight silver medal

        12       at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics.  He earned his

        13       first boxing paycheck serving as a sparring

        14       partner for Sugar Ray Robinson in 1957; and

        15                  "WHEREAS, Early in his pro career,

        16       Jose Torres became friendly with young

        17       writers, among them Pete Hamill, who was with

        18       the New York Post.  Pete Hamill helped Jose

        19       Torres get a column in the paper, and Jose

        20       wrote often on Latino community affairs; and

        21                  "WHEREAS, When Jose Torres was

        22       introduced as the state athletic commissioner

        23       in November of 1984 by Governor Mario Cuomo,

        24       his guests included Cus D'Amato, his former



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         243



         1       manager; Pete Hamill; Budd Schulberg, who

         2       wrote the epilogue to the Ali biography; and

         3       Norman Mailer; and

         4                  "WHEREAS, Jose Torres cited Cus

         5       D'Amato as 'the man who created the fighter'

         6       and Norman Mailer as 'the man who created my

         7       intellectual capacity.'  Jose vowed that as

         8       chairman of the athletic commission, he would

         9       promote educational opportunities for fighters

        10       'at least so they can read their contracts';

        11       and

        12                  "WHEREAS, Jose Torres, a member of

        13       the athletic commission before becoming its

        14       chairman, had also been active in societal

        15       affairs, working for Paul O'Dwyer when he was

        16       the president of New York's City Council and

        17       for Andrew Stein when he was the Manhattan

        18       borough president; and

        19                  "WHEREAS, Jose Torres distinguished

        20       himself in his profession by his sincere

        21       dedication and substantial contribution to the

        22       welfare of his community; and

        23                  "WHEREAS, Jose Torres' commitment

        24       to excellence, and his spirit of humanity,



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         244



         1       carried over into all fields of enterprise,

         2       including charitable and civic endeavors; and

         3                  "WHEREAS, Jose Torres is survived

         4       by his wife, Ramonita; now, therefore, be it

         5                  "RESOLVED, That this Legislative

         6       Body pause in its deliberations to mourn the

         7       death of Boxing Hall of Famer and Ambassador

         8       Jose Torres, distinguished citizen and devoted

         9       member of his community; and be it further

        10                  "RESOLVED, That copies of this

        11       resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted

        12       to the family of Jose Torres."

        16       President.  I rise to honor the memory of a

        17       distinguished gentleman and human being.

        18                  Mr. "Chegui" Torres was an unsung

        19       hero, but definitely he was a hero in the

        20       Latino and Puerto Rican community.  As the

        21       resolution indicates, he definitely

        22       distinguished himself in many professional

        23       areas.

        24                  And I'd really like to publicly

         1       offer my sympathies to his family, and my

         2       condolences, and thank them for his many years

         5       this resolution be opened up to all members.

        10                  SENATOR ADAMS:    Thank you,

        11       Madam President.  I too rise to show my

        12       support for our great fighter Torres and to

        13       really reflect on how he was a historical,

        14       historical figure.

        15                  At the beginning of the year -- as

        16       we talk about historical figures, at the

        17       beginning of the year I did a little

        18       unscientific survey where I brought an old

        19       survey that was done many years ago with two

        20       dolls, one of the dolls being black and one of

        21       the dolls being white.  And I went to a public

        22       school, and I held the dolls up and I asked

        23       the students in the classroom -- young

        24       children, second- and third-graders -- which



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         246



         1       one of the dolls were smart.  Eighty percent

         2       of the children said the white doll was

         3       smarter than the black doll.

         4                  After the Obama race, I returned to

         5       the school and I held up the dolls again, and

         6       it turned to 60/40 where the students said the

         7       black doll was smarter than the white doll.

         8                  So the concern is not so much who

         9       is brighter or who's not, but it's to shatter

        10       myths and misconceptions.

        11                  And as we stand here in this

        12       chamber feeling the residue of the Obama

        13       election, we once again see a first, by having

        14       you stand and adorn our Senate environment.

        15       So you now are, just as Obama, the first woman

        16       and person of color to stand in that position

        17       as the Temporary President and the President

        18       of the Senate, and we commend you for that.

        19                  We are in a major point in our

        20       lives as Americans that we start the process

        21       of becoming modern-day Johnnie Appleseeds and

        22       planting the seeds of prosperity and

        23       opportunity everywhere from the tip of the

        24       state to the bottom of the state.



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.

         1                  And I believe that not only has the

         2       wave of Obamamania taken over the country to

         3       breathe change into our lungs so that we can

         4       have the energy, the capacity to blow the

         5       state in the direction that it ought to go

         6       into, but that change also has found its way

         7       into the State Senate.

         8                  You are doing a great job.  We're

         9       happy to see you here.  And little children

        10       all over the country will see that they too

        11       can aspire to be not only a great senator but

        12       to stand in front of this great conference and

        13       do great things for this state and this

        14       country.

        15                  Thank you.

        24       and thank Senator Dilan for bringing this

         1       resolution to this floor.

         2                  As a fan of boxing, I have always

         3       been aware of the great career of Jose Torres.

         4       But I think what's even more fascinating about

         5       this amazing person was his career outside of

         6       the ring.

         7                  In a time when we see many athletes

         8       having a very hard time coming to grips with

         9       the fact that their athletic career may be

        10       over and having little to do after that, Jose

        11       Torres showed that his exploits in the ring

        12       were only part of the tremendous wealth of

        13       knowledge and opportunity that he presented

        14       not only to the Latino community, to the

        15       Puerto Rican community, but to all

        16       communities.

        17                  We lost a great person.  We lost a

        18       great man.  Someone who inspired us through

        19       his exploits in the ring as well as the things

        20       he wrote in his books and memoirs.  He was an

        21       advisor to a tremendous champion such as Mike

        22       Tyson and well-respected throughout the sport.

        23                  I think that as we look to role

        24       models and we look to people to try to

         5       Dilan.
